title: Constructible sheaves
statement:
In this subsection $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, so $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and we can argue with constructible
cohomology sheaves and standard truncations. A $\Lambda_X$-module is constructible
([sk-def-sfb-constructible]) exactly when it is *lisse*, that is locally free of finite rank
for the pro-étale topology, on each stratum of a finite stratification of $X$. For a locally
closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$, factor $a=i\circ u$ with
$u\colon S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ the open immersion into the closure and
$i\colon\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ the closed immersion, and put
$a_!=i_*u_!\colon\Mod(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$. Both $u_!$
and $i_*$ are exact, so $a_!$ is exact, and it induces
$a_!\colon D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ without deriving.

Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, and let $X$ be a standing scheme.

1. $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions in
   $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$. In particular it is an abelian category, and its
   inclusion into $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ is exact.
2. $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is essentially small.
3. Every $F\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ has a finite filtration $0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_m=F$
   whose subquotients $F_k/F_{k-1}$ are of the form $a_!L$, with $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$
   a locally closed immersion and $L$ a lisse $\Lambda_S$-module.

For a curve $X$, part (3) says that a constructible sheaf $F$ sits in an exact sequence
$0\to u_!L\to F\to i_*G\to0$, where $u$ is the inclusion of a dense open subset on which $F$
is lisse, $L=u^*F$, and $i_*G$ is supported on the finitely many closed points of the
complement.

external.place: *Kernels and cokernels.* On the topologically Noetherian scheme $S$, the kernel and cokernel of a morphism of lisse $\Lambda_S$-modules are lisse (Bhatt–Scholze, *The pro-étale topology for schemes*, Corollary 6.8.5); in particular its rank is locally constant on $S$, and no further stratification is needed.

*Kernels and cokernels.* On the topologically Noetherian scheme $S$, the kernel and cokernel of a morphism of lisse $\Lambda_S$-modules are lisse (Bhatt–Scholze, *The pro-étale topology for schemes*, Corollary 6.8.5); in particular its rank is locally constant on $S$, and no further stratification is needed.

proof.text: The standing finite-type-over-a-field setting is [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Its schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to the structure morphism to the spectrum of a field (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and itself). Open subschemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Closed subschemes are locally Noetherian because their affine rings are quotients of Noetherian rings: an ascending chain of quotient ideals lifts to one in the original ring. They are quasi-compact as closed subsets of a quasi-compact space. Factoring a locally closed immersion as closed into an open therefore shows that its source is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], the underlying spaces are topologically Noetherian. Every open subset is quasi-compact: otherwise a cover without a finite subcover gives, by successively adding a member, a strictly increasing chain of opens, contradicting the descending condition on their closed complements. Applying this inside each open subset proves that open immersions are quasi-compact. We use coefficient module sheaves, not sheaves over the discrete constant field: [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] identifies $E_X$ with $\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]$ and $\QbarX$ with $\varinjlim_E E_X$.

source.place: Standing hypotheses and identification of coefficient sheaves; introductory paragraph

proof.text: The finite constant local models defining constructibility are those in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Over the scalar field $\Lambda(*)$, a finitely presented module is a finite-dimensional vector space, hence isomorphic to $\Lambda(*)^r$; extending scalars gives $\Lambda_U^r$. Conversely $\Lambda_U^r$ comes from the finite free scalar module. Therefore constructible means lisse on a finite stratification, as asserted also in [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure]. The preliminary equality $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)=\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is the field case of [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc]: every bounded constructible complex has finite Tor amplitude. Standard truncations have the same cohomology sheaves in a smaller finite range and zero elsewhere, so remain bounded constructible.

source.place: Preliminary paragraph: local models, lisseness, and finite Tor amplitude

proof.text: For $a=i\circ u$ through the closure, use the module extension by zero $u_!$ of [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. The coefficient identifications and exact inverse image are [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with ring sheaf $\Lambda_X$ to $i$ and its complementary open: $i_*$ is exact, since that open is quasi-compact by step 1. The same node gives exactness of $u_!$. Consequently $a_!=i_*u_!$ is exact. Applied to a complex $K$, exactness gives $H^n(a_!K)=a_!H^n(K)$, by preserving the kernel and image of each differential. It therefore preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends to the localization $D(S,\Lambda)\to D(X,\Lambda)$, without taking a resolution.

source.place: Preliminary paragraph: locally closed extension by zero; Stacks Tags 09BM and 03DJ

proof.text: For a morphism $F\to G$ of constructible sheaves, choose a common adapted stratification by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification](1),(2). Restriction to each stratum is exact by its part (3), so the restrictions of the ambient kernel and cokernel are the kernel and cokernel of the restricted morphism. On each Noetherian stratum the source and target are lisse. Part (2) of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure] makes these restricted kernels and cokernels lisse. They are therefore constructible on $X$ by the criterion in step 2. This uses the actual local kernel/cokernel assertion, not just the definition of lisse or a claim about ranks.

source.place: Part (1), kernels and cokernels; Bhatt–Scholze Corollary 6.8.5

proof.text: For $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ with $F',F''$ constructible, choose a common adapted stratification for the two end terms using [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification]. Its exact restriction gives an extension of lisse modules on every stratum. Part (1) of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure] makes the middle module lisse on that stratum; explicitly, locally trivialize the end terms and lift the finitely many basis sections of the quotient after refining the cover, giving a local splitting and a finite free middle term. Thus $F$ is constructible. The final assertion of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure] now gives that this full subcategory is abelian with exact inclusion. Its zero object is the rank-zero sheaf, and finite direct sums are constructible by the split extension $0\to A\to A\oplus B\to B\to0$.

source.place: Part (1), extensions and the abelian subcategory

proof.text: Fix the universe for the sites and coefficient modules. The hypotheses of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-small] hold: $X$ is Noetherian and $\Lambda$ is one of the two specified fields. That statement supplies a set of isomorphism classes of constructible sheaves. Selecting one representative of each gives a small full subcategory equivalent to $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, which is precisely essential smallness. This citation includes the required control of gluing between strata; separate descent data on the strata alone would not determine the global sheaf.

source.place: Part (2): essential smallness and its detailed lemma

proof.text: Choose an adapted stratification of $F$ and refine and order it by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification](1),(2), so $V_k=S_1\cup\cdots\cup S_k$ is open. The hypotheses of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-filtration] hold: $X$ is Noetherian by step 1, $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, and $F$ is constructible on this ordered adapted stratification. With $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$, its current statement gives subsheaves $F_k=v_{k!}v_k^*F$, endpoints $F_0=0$ and $F_m=F$, and $F_k/F_{k-1}\cong a_{k!}(F|_{S_k})$, with each $F|_{S_k}$ lisse. Its definition of $a_{k!}$ is exactly $i_*u_!$ through the closure, as in this item and step 3, so these are the requested subquotients for the specified functor. The inclusions in a finite filtration need not be strict: the item’s $\subset$ notation is read as subsheaf inclusion. For $F=0$ all terms can be zero, and for $X=\varnothing$ the empty filtration has $m=0$. Thus the added non-strict-inclusion convention in the cited statement preserves the claimed filtration, including these edge cases.

source.place: Part (3): ordered stratification and explicit filtration

proof.text: For the curve assertion, there are finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Each component $C$ has a unique generic point $\eta$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Let $S$ be its adapted stratum. Write $S=O\cap D$ with $O$ open and $D$ closed. Since $\eta\in D$, one has $C\subseteq D$. Removing the other components from $O$ gives an open neighborhood $W_\eta$ of $\eta$ in $X$ contained in $C\cap O\subseteq S$. Here containment in $S$ is initially set-theoretic. Put $T=W_\eta\times_X S$: $T\to W_\eta$ is a surjective closed immersion, and $F|_T$ is lisse by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification](2). To infer lisseness on $W_\eta$ without assuming reducedness, apply [new-lem-weil-pbc-proetale-surjective-closed-cover-refinement] to a pro-étale trivializing cover of $T$. It gives a pro-étale cover $\{B_b\to W_\eta\}$ whose closed base changes $T_b=B_b\times_{W_\eta}T$ map to members of that trivializing cover; hence $F|_{T_b}$ is finite free. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to $T_b\to B_b$ with empty complementary open. Its short exact sequence gives $M\simeq i_*i^*M$ for every module sheaf $M$, and its counit gives $i^*i_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Thus restriction is an equivalence of module categories. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], it sends $\Lambda_{B_b}^r$ to $\Lambda_{T_b}^r$. Full faithfulness therefore lifts the isomorphism $F|_{T_b}\simeq\Lambda_{T_b}^r$ and its inverse to an isomorphism $F|_{B_b}\simeq\Lambda_{B_b}^r$. This proves that $F$ is lisse on $W_\eta$. Their union $U$ is dense and $L=F|_U$ is lisse, because lisseness is local for open covers. The closed complement $Z$ contains no generic point of a component. It has dimension at most zero: a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets in $Z$, extended to a component of $X$, would otherwise give a chain of length at least two in a curve. The underlying space of $X$ is Noetherian by step 1 and is $T_0$: if two points have the same closure, both are generic points of that irreducible closed subset, so [lem-sc-scheme-sober] makes them equal. Thus [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-closed-finite] applies to the closed subset $Z$ and gives finitely many points, all closed in $X$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], with $u:U\hookrightarrow X$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, and $G=i^*F$, gives $0\to u_!L\to F\to i_*G\to0$. Its identity $u^*i_*=0$ shows the last term is supported on $Z$. No algebraic closedness of the ground field, smoothness, or irreducibility is needed.
